item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is preferable because it leaves the lower-level Add API unchanged and implements explicit Upload validation with the established multipart helper. Its main flaw is duplicating Add instead of delegating to it.","reasons":["A materially changes Add by eagerly reading every custom multipart body into memory, altering streaming, memory use, and reader-error timing despite the contract requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged.","B explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before request construction, then propagates multipartbody.NewFile errors.","Both reuse internal/multipartbody.NewFile and appear to produce replayable Upload bodies, but neither follows the explicit requirement to call FilesService.Add.","A has substantially better retry verification: its Upload test parses and checks field name, filename, and content on both attempts, whereas B's retry test never consumes the request body."],"risks_a":["The new io.ReadAll in Add can cause large memory usage for callers intentionally using streamed custom multipart bodies.","Upload bypasses Add through a private add helper, and the changelog advertises an out-of-scope Add behavior change.","No visible Upload tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failure."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors, creating drift risk and directly violating the required delegation pattern.","The Upload test checks the multipart filename but never reads or verifies the uploaded content.","The retry test only counts transport calls; its fake transport does not read either request body, so it does not prove replay correctness or test Upload end to end—nor are validation and reader failures visibly tested."]}
